source.title: Two to Tango: Coupled Task-Reference Selection for Safe LLM Fine-tuning
source.authors: Xin-Rui Chen; Jian-Hao Zhang; Ou Wu; Dian-Lei Gao

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper develops a fine-tuning defense motivated by safety degradation and reports its safety performance. It does not test the claim versions about few-example harmful or benign fine-tuning, first-token concentration, opening-token bypasses, localized safety parameters, causes of shallowness, or deepening safety.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates safety after fine-tuning and reports unsafe-completion rates, but does not compare them with the aligned model before fine-tuning or isolate the effects of harmful versus benign examples. It reports no per-token KL analysis, compliant-prefix, suffix or decoding intervention, parameter-localization test, or safety-deepening test. Results cited from prior work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: DualSelect is a safe fine-tuning defense. The paper cites Qi et al. 2024 as motivation for fine-tuning eroding safety, then reports only how its method compares with baselines. It reports no ASR for the aligned checkpoint before fine-tuning, so post-fine-tuning ASR cannot show erosion. It has no per-token KL, prefill/suffix/decoding attack, parameter-localization or deepening test.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that DualSelect better preserves safety than baselines on REDORCA and GSM8K, with comparable utility, moderate overhead and limited over-refusal. They make no finding on token depth or the other versions.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies coupled selection of task samples and safe-response references, plus reference-gradient correction; it does not apply the original claim's few-example fine-tuning or token-position measurement recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported safety outcomes vary by fine-tuning method and dataset. The absolute ASR comparison in Table 10 is for Llama-3-8B-Instruct on REDORCA; the paper also reports broader safety averages across models, datasets, and judges.

fits_no_version.finding: Safety-preserving fine-tuning methods give lower post-fine-tuning ASR than Standard SFT on REDORCA. DualSelect is at 15.8% versus 52.8% for Standard SFT (Table 10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-conditioned safety-reference selection during fine-tuning lowers post-fine-tuning unsafe completion relative to standard SFT.

record.problems: The absolute ASR results are reported without uncertainty values. The study does not report an ASR baseline for the aligned model before fine-tuning, so the table does not establish how much fine-tuning itself changed ASR. Safety evaluation partly uses automatic judges or detectors; the authors state human evaluation is future work.
record.rows_left_out: Other safety metrics, including pairwise Safety Avg., harmfulness scores, and false-refusal rates, were not extracted as rows because they do not directly report the claim's harmful-compliance measure. Results cited from prior work and figure-only results were also omitted.

untested.parts: No pre-fine-tuning ASR and no few-to-few-hundred harmful-example fine-tuning.
GSM8K Standard SFT ASR (38.4%) is given without the aligned model's ASR, so erosion from benign data is not shown.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks.
No localization of safety in parameters.
No test of causes of shallowness.
No training that deepens safety beyond early tokens.

record.verdict_notes: Table 10 also gives GSM8K absolute ASR (Standard SFT 38.4%) after benign math fine-tuning, which rows omit. With no pre-fine-tuning baseline it cannot bear on V2. The main safety metrics are win rates against Standard SFT, not compliance rates.

versions.untested_parts: Does not isolate fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred harmful examples or test whether such examples cause compliance.
Does not measure whether ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance relative to the aligned starting model.
No per-token KL comparison between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding-change bypass tests.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
No test of whether training data or the training objective produces shallow safety.
No test of training that spreads safety beyond initial response tokens or whether such deepening holds up.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B-Instruct
rows.note: Absolute safety evaluation after fine-tuning; no ASR for the aligned starting checkpoint is reported.
rows.check: Standard SFT ASR of 52.8% after REDORCA fine-tuning is absolute, with no pre-fine-tuning aligned baseline. It cannot show erosion for V1 or V2. REDORCA also mixes benign instructions with red-teaming pairs, so the harmful/benign split is not isolated.
